text:
Maya: Quick sync — drafting an onboarding headroom shim for Dedicated customers. Need product + eng alignment on default onboarding buffer, whether it's refundable, and launch gates. Proposal below.

Jon: +1. Can you call out customer scenarios (low-commit vs enterprise)?

Maya: Yep. Proposal (rough):
```
onboard_headroom:
  default_pct: 20
  refundable: false
  carryover_window_days: 30
  min_gpu_floor: 0.25
```

Eli: 20% feels high for small tenants. What does that map to in GPUs/tokens?

Maya: For a small reserved pool (4g), 20% ≈ 0.8g reserved for 14d. We can add a floor so tiny customers don't hit weird fractions (see min_gpu_floor).

Alicia: Launch gates we care about: console visibility for headroom usage, billing reconciliation, SLA docs, and opt-out flow. No GA until docs + legal check.

Samir: Ops note: autoscale must respect tenant-level onboarding headroom before returning capacity to shared burst. If not, cross-tenant noisy neighbor risk increases.

capacity-bot: FYI — current autoscale policy enforces headroom at pool-level. Tenant-level headroom is feature-flagged and on dev backlog.

Jon: Technical take — we can do tenant-level reservation but it affects packing heuristics. Suggest a split: default_pct=10 for low-commit customers, 20 for enterprise.

Maya: Tradeoffs: lower % reduces friction but ups chance of preemptions. Proposed acceptance criteria for GA:
- <1% cross-tenant preemptions attributable to onboarding headroom in first 30d
- Headroom usage surfaced in Console per-tenant and in billing export
- Canary rollout with observability and rollback playbook

Eli: Rollout suggestion: stage 1 canary (50 tenants, 2 weeks), stage 2: 10% of new onboardings for 30d, monitor headroom churn and latency impact.

Alicia: Docs owners: I can draft "What customers see" + opt-out UX. Legal: please review refundable vs non-refundable language.

Samir: Sales ops ask: refundable headroom helps close deals but adds billing complexity. If non-refundable, we should offer an explicit credit flow for exceptional cases.

Maya: Decision proposal: non-refundable for GA, telemetry-led revisit after 90d. Action items: @Jon scope eng work, @Eli build dashboards & evals, @Alicia docs + legal.

Jon: I'll open an RFC for tenant-headroom-shim with implementation plan and perf impact. ETA: EOW.

Eli: I'll add a dashboard tile and an eval harness to detect regressions in tail latency when headroom is applied.

deploy-bot: maya triggered rollout-plan/create canary — status: queued

Maya: Thanks — reconvene in 48h assuming RFCs/drafts are up. :party_parrot:
